items.review_rationale: Examined the count of distinct roots of an irreducible polynomial in an algebraic closure of the coefficient field, distinguishing separable degree from its usual polynomial degree and from extension degree.

references.context: Field theory: irreducible polynomial in the univariate polynomial ring F[x]

references.phrase: roots of a polynomial in a field
references.context: Field theory: root of polynomial f, an element α with f(α)=0

references.disposition: Distinct-root cardinality is used; repeated roots of f count once, and no general equality with the polynomial degree is assumed.

items.review_rationale: Read the two equivalent characterizations in their field-coefficient context: the formal derivative is coprime to f, equivalently no repeated roots in an algebraic closure. Do not conflate a zero derivative with separability.

references.phrase: relatively prime polynomials f and f′

references.context: Field theory: irreducible polynomial over a field
Polynomial algebra: formal derivative of a univariate polynomial, including positive characteristic
Field theory: multiple root or multiplicity of polynomial root over an algebraic closure

references.disposition: The coprimality criterion and no-repeated-root property concern the same polynomial; no irreducibility condition on f′ is required.

items.review_rationale: Inspected both inclusion and injective-field-homomorphism presentations. The image of the homomorphism is identified with a subfield; E and F are fields, not merely rings with injections.

references.context: Field theory: subset of a field closed under field operations and multiplicative inverses of nonzero elements

references.disposition: This is the equivalence up to field isomorphism of the two stated extension conventions, not a claim about an arbitrary noninjective ring map.

items.review_rationale: Read the finite chain of nested fields and checked that the extension E_i/E_{i−1} is taken in the displayed ascending direction; finite tower length does not mean finite degree of its steps.

references.disposition: The number of nested fields is finite, but each field extension may have infinite degree and need not be algebraic.

items.review_rationale: Read the inverse-limit characterization of profinite spaces and preserved its use of finite discrete spaces and homeomorphism, rather than merely an inverse system or product of finite spaces.

references.context: Topology: finite sets equipped with discrete topology, with continuous transition maps

references.disposition: An inverse limit is taken with compatible transition maps; no directedness or surjectivity beyond what an inverse system requires is asserted.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed the precise equivalence for profinite spaces: quasicompact, Hausdorff and totally disconnected. All three conditions are required, with no additional local connectedness assumption.

references.disposition: The conjunction characterizes profinite spaces under the given convention and is not simply compactness or total disconnectedness in isolation.

items.review_rationale: Read the embedded-associated-prime criterion relative to the associated prime set of M. Its nonminimality is among associated primes under inclusion, not among all prime ideals of the ring.

references.phrase: associated prime p of an R-module M
minimal under inclusion among associated primes
references.context: Order theory: minimal element of the subset Ass_R(M) ordered by inclusion

references.disposition: The criterion negates minimality inside Ass_R(M), not inside Spec(R) or the annihilator's complete collection of primes.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed the embedded-prime ring convention, which applies the module-associated-prime notion to R acting on itself. It does not mean simply a nonminimal prime in the full prime spectrum.

references.phrase: embedded associated prime of an R-module

references.disposition: The module action here is regular multiplication in R and introduces no second choice of an external module.
